conflicts.subject: Whether iOS 9.2.1 had a third numbered public-beta appearance

positions.summary: The final-release report says developers and public testers received three betas in total.
The retained exact chronology exposes Public Beta 1 on December 17 and Public Beta 2 on January 4, with no exact Public Beta 3 identity.

decision.rationale: An aggregate count cannot supply a missing event identity, date, or displayed label. The direct numbered reports control until exact contrary evidence appears.

conflicts.reversalEvidence: A contemporary source that explicitly identifies iOS 9.2.1 Public Beta 3, its availability date, and its public audience.

conflicts.subject: Whether the untimestamped update on the September 30 MacRumors article establishes the public appearance date

positions.summary: MacRumors appended the public-audience statement to a September 30 article without displaying a separate update time.
9to5Mac independently published and updated its public-beta report on September 30.

decision.rationale: The independent same-day report removes the date ambiguity while preserving Public Beta 3 as a separate audience appearance.

conflicts.subject: Whether one build can represent the iOS 9.1 Public Beta 5 appearance

positions.summary: The report identifies one public build for the general device set and another for the newly released iPhone models.
The audience appearance is unambiguous even though one unqualified build value would be misleading.

decision.rationale: Build variants require device-qualified modeling. The chronology candidate records the public appearance only.

conflicts.subject: Whether iOS 9.3 developer Beta 1.1 creates a public Beta 1.1 event

positions.summary: The retained cycle evidence identifies Beta 1.1 as a developer repair seed.
The public-program report labels the January 14 distribution as the first public beta, not Public Beta 1.1.

decision.rationale: Developer revision labels do not transfer to the public channel without explicit public-channel evidence.

conflicts.reversalEvidence: A public-program source explicitly displaying Public Beta 1.1 as a separate public appearance.

conflicts.subject: Misleading developer-focused URL slugs or body copy on iCulture's iOS 9.2 Public Beta 2 and Public Beta 4 reports

positions.summary: The legacy slugs mention developers, and the Public Beta 2 lead retains developer-focused copy.
The retained rendered headlines explicitly label the second and fourth releases for public testers on the candidate dates.

decision.rationale: A legacy URL slug is not an event label. The rendered publisher headline explicitly identifies the public audience and ordinal, while the mismatch remains documented.

conflicts.subject: Whether iOS 9.3.2 Public Beta 1 appeared on the developer article's April 6 publication date or its April 7 public update

positions.summary: The original article and headline identify the first developer seed on April 6.
The retained article has an explicit April 7 update saying iOS 9.3.2 became available as a public beta.

decision.rationale: Developer and public audience appearances are separate events. The explicitly dated public update controls the public chronology.

conflicts.reversalEvidence: A contemporary public-program source explicitly showing availability before April 7, 2016.

conflicts.subject: Stale developer-only or future-tense paragraphs within same-day revised iCulture pages for iOS 9.3.3 Public Beta 1 and Public Beta 3

positions.summary: Later page paragraphs still say the public release will follow or describe only developer availability.
The rendered headline or lead explicitly says the first or third public beta is available, and JSON-LD records a same-day modification.

decision.rationale: The revision-specific text is direct public-availability evidence; the internally stale paragraphs are preserved so downstream reviewers can reproduce the source history.

excludedAppearances.reason: A public bug-fix release is not a public beta; no exact public-beta appearance was found or inferred.
Public security releases are not repurposed as beta events.

excludedAppearances.identity: Revised public builds of iOS 9.2.1 and iOS 9.3
excludedAppearances.reason: A revised final public payload is not a public-beta appearance.
